q: Can I deduct carbon credits I bought from my Scope 1 and 2 totals in BRSR or for a buyer?
title: Can carbon credits reduce my Scope 1 and 2?
short: No. Report Scope 1 and Scope 2 gross, as emitted, and show carbon credits you bought and retired as a separate line. The GHG Protocol keeps offsets outside the inventory, BRSR asks for gross emissions, and a buyer adding your figures to its Scope 3 needs gross figures too.
audience: Listed companies, their value chain and exporters

p: The Corporate Standard treats offsets as outside the inventory. A company can report credits it has bought or retired, but as separate information, not subtracted from Scope 1, 2 or 3. The inventory describes what your operations emitted; a credit describes a reduction somewhere else.

ul: Principle 6 asks for total Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and intensity. Enter gross figures.

SEBI's March 2025 circular added a voluntary leadership indicator for Green Credits under the Green Credit Rules, 2023. That is a count of Green Credits, not carbon credits, and it is not netted against emissions either.
If you retired carbon credits, describe them in a note: registry, project, vintage, quantity and retirement serial numbers.

p: A buyer uses your Scope 1 and 2 to build its own Scope 3. If you send a net figure, its inventory understates what was emitted. Send gross figures and, if you want, add a note on credits retired. Net claims such as carbon neutral are a separate, governed claim and need their own evidence.

sections.h: The one look-alike that is allowed
p: Renewable energy instruments are different from carbon credits. RECs, a green tariff or a qualifying PPA can lower your market-based Scope 2, because they describe the electricity you bought, under the Scope 2 Guidance. Report location-based Scope 2 alongside. A carbon credit can never be used this way.

example.title: Worked example: how to present it
lines: Scope 1: 300 t CO2e; Scope 2 location-based: 200 t CO2; total 500 t, reported gross
Carbon credits retired for the year: 200 t CO2e, shown separately with registry and serial numbers
Wrong: reporting 300 t as Scope 1 and 2 after deducting credits
Right: 500 t gross, plus a separate line for 200 credits retired

senseible: Senseible reports gross emissions from your documents and does not net carbon credits against them. Credits you hold sit apart from the inventory.
